lines.text: Twelve units of fence, bent once, tucked into a corner.
lines.caption: Twelve units of fence, bent once, tucked into a corner.

lines.text: Most kids make a square. But a square is NOT the best!
lines.caption: Most kids make a square. But a square is NOT the best!

lines.text: Two walls meet at a right angle. A two-piece fence, total length twelve, joins them.
lines.caption: Two walls meet at a right angle. A two-piece fence, total length twelve, joins them.

lines.text: What's the largest area it can enclose?
lines.caption: What's the largest area it can enclose?

lines.text: Here's the trick. Treat each wall like a mirror.
lines.caption: Here's the trick. Treat each wall like a mirror.

lines.text: Reflect the region across both walls, and the corner disappears.
lines.caption: Reflect the region across both walls, and the corner disappears.

lines.text: Now the fence is a closed octagon, four times our area.
lines.caption: Now the fence is a closed octagon, four times our area.

lines.text: The best octagon is the regular one. And our fence makes it!
lines.caption: The best octagon is the regular one. And our fence makes it!

lines.text: Our region is a quarter of it. The answer is <short pause> Choice B!
lines.caption: Our region is a quarter of it. The answer is Choice B!

lines.text: About forty-three and a half. The square only gets thirty-six!
lines.caption: About forty-three and a half. The square only gets thirty-six!
